source_text: Ναί, φασίν. Eἰ οὖν ἡ σὰρξ ἀνίσταται, καὶ τοιαύτη ἀνίσταται ὁποία κλιθήσεται, ὥστε, εἰ μονόφθαλμος κλιθήσεται, μονόφθαλμος ἀνίσταται, εἰ χωλός, χωλός, εἰ ἄλλο τι τοῦ σώματος ὑστεροῦν εἴη, τοῦτο καὶ ἐλάττων ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἀναστήσεται. Τετυφλωμένοι ὡς ἀληθῶς τὰ τῆς καρδίας ὄμματα! Oὐ γὰρ εἶδον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς τυφλοὺς ἀναβλέποντας, χωλοὺς περιπατοῦντας τῷ ἐκείνου λόγῳ; Ἂ πάντα ἐποίησεν ὁ σωτήρ, πρῶτον μὲν ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ·ηθὲν περὶ αὐτοῦ διὰ τῶν προφητῶν, ὅτι Τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσι καὶ κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν καὶ τὰ ἄλλα, ἔτι δὲ καὶ εἰς πίστιν τοῦ ὅτι ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ἡ σὰρξ ὁλόκληρος ἀναστήσεται. Eἰ γὰρ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς τὰς ἀσθενείας τῆς σαρκὸς ἰάσατο καὶ ὁλόκληρον ἐποίησε τὸ σῶμα, πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τοῦτο ποιήσει, ὥστε καὶ ἀκέραιον καὶ ὁλόκληρον ἀναστῆναι τὴν σάρκα. Τὰ μὲν οὖν παρ' αὐτῶν νομιζόμενα ἄπορα τοῦτον τὸν τρόπον ἰαθήσεται.
pass_a_gloss: Yes, they say. If then the flesh rises, and it rises such as it was laid, so that if it was laid blind in one eye, it rises blind in one eye, if it was lame, it rises lame, if some other part of the body was lacking, this also the person rises inferior. Blind as to the true eyes of the heart! For they did not see on the earth blind people recovering their sight, lame people walking about by His word? All things the Savior did, first in order that what was spoken about Him through the prophets might be fulfilled, that Blind people recover their sight and deaf people hear and the other things, and yet also for faith that in the resurrection the flesh rises whole. For if on the earth He healed the weaknesses of the flesh and made the body whole, much more in the resurrection He will do this, so that the flesh also rises whole and complete. The things then considered impossible by them will be healed in this way.

pass_b_english: Yes, they say. If the flesh rises, then it rises exactly as it was laid down—so that if it was laid down blind in one eye, it rises blind in one eye; if lame, it rises lame; if any other part of the body was lacking, the person rises still inferior because of that. How blind the true eyes of their hearts are! Did they not see on earth blind people recovering their sight and lame people walking by His word? The Savior did all these things, first so that what was spoken about Him through the prophets might be fulfilled—that the blind receive sight and the deaf hear, and the other things (Isaiah 35:5)—and also to give faith that in the resurrection the flesh will rise whole. For if on earth He healed the weaknesses of the flesh and made the body whole, how much more will He do this in the resurrection, so that the flesh also rises whole and complete. In this way the things they regard as impossible will be healed.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text, including the conditional clauses regarding physical defects and the theological argument for the resurrection. Pass B correctly identifies the prophetic allusion as Isaiah 35:5, which matches the Greek content 'Τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσι καὶ κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν'.
